text:
dana: incident-bot paging ops-oncall: GPU pool spike and autoscaler failures in prod-east :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Paging @kai (oncall), incident created: GPU_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTION - thread 1763401200
kai: I’m on it, pulling logs now. any customer-facing alerts?
dana: Yes, spike in 429s reported by the gateway around 14:03 UTC. Dashboard shows queued requests ballooning on /v1/generate routes.
sara: I’m seeing queue length > 12k in the request router, sustained. Per-route throttling kicking in (503/429). Most affected: customer accounts with heavy batch inference (embedding jobs).
kai: Checking node events and cluster-autoscaler logs.
ops-bot: autoscaler: failed scale-up attempt at 14:04:03 - reason: reached maxNodes for ASG (max=150, desired=150)
kai: autoscaler hit ASG max. That explains no new nodes. But why do we have stranded GPU capacity?
dana: Some nodes show GPUs with available memory but pods pending with InsufficientGPU allocatable. suspicion: MIG fragmentation / wrong resource requests.
mike: Pasting `kubectl describe pod` for one pending pod:
```
Name: embedder-xyz
Status: Pending
Events:
  Type    Reason              Age    From               Message
  ----    ------              ----   ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling    2m     default-scheduler  0/120 nodes are available: 120 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
```

kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU_ALLOC:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu,GPU_CAP:.status.capacity.nvidia.com/gpu,ALLOCATABLE_MEM:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/memory
node-3   0.25      1   8192
node-4   0.25      1   8192
node-5   1         1   16384

anya: Wait nodes showing `allocatable` 0.25 GPUs — that's MIG profiles on the GPU. A lot of nodes have small fractional GPUs available; our pod requests are for 1 whole GPU. Binpacking mismatch.
kai: So fragmentation: cluster has many MIG-sliced GPUs (e.g., 4x0.25) and some full GPUs. Scheduler thinks there's enough total capacity but not contiguous whole GPUs for 1 GPU requests. That leads to stranded fractional capacity.
sara: Also noticed autoscaler launches use a mix of node types: some nodegroups are configured with MIG-enabled images and set to profile 7g. Others are full GPUs. Scale group capacity per nodegroup is limited and the autoscaler is not aware of fragmentation.
dana: Customer impact: 12 customers reported degraded throughput and higher latency; SLA alerts fired for two enterprise tenants. Support has opened CS tickets.
kai: Immediate mitigation plan:
  1) Start fallbacks: temporarily route heavy batch jobs to a smaller, less efficient CPU-based async queue (embedding fallback) to relieve GPU queue pressure. (Sara + Support)
  2) Launch manual scale-up in a nodegroup that has full GPUs (if quota allows) — bypassing autoscaler. (Mike)
  3) Reconfigure scheduler/dispatcher to accept fractional-GPU capable workloads for certain lighter models. (Anya + Eng-ml)
  4) Investigate nodegroup max limits and request quota bump for ASG in prod-east. (Kai + Infra)

sara: Actioning (1) now: enabling fallback for embeddings queue; telling gateway to shift traffic. This should lower queued GPU-bound load within 3-5 min.
mike: Trying manual scale: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name asg-gpu-prod-full --desired-capacity 12` -> response OK. Creating two full-GPU nodes (if scheduler places them).
ops-bot: cloud: new instances provisioning in asg-gpu-prod-full (2 instances)
kai: While nodes spin up, we should also look for quick wins: evict low-priority jobs currently holding whole GPUs that can be preempted. Any preemptible pool?
dana: Yes, we have a low-priority batch pool (label: priority=batch-low). I’ll cordon a couple of nodes that are running low-priority jobs and trigger graceful eviction.
anya: FYI, a lot of the MIG-enabled nodes have GPU slice sizes set to 0.25 and pod resource model was recently changed to request whole GPUs for compatibility. We need to support fractional requests or reprofile MIG to larger slices for binpacking. That's medium-term.
sara: Fallback in place: gateway shows reduced /v1/generate rate to GPU pool. Pending queue dropping from 12k -> 6k in 2 min. :thumbsup:
mike: New full-GPU nodes came up and joined cluster at 14:11. Kube-scheduler assigned 18 waiting pods onto them. Pod startup errors minimal.
kai: Great. Keep monitoring. Need to flip autoscaler config: node affinity rules for scale-up must prefer full-gpu nodegroup for requests needing whole GPU. Also file to adjust cluster-autoscaler expander strategy to prefer largest instance first.
dana: Observed one strange thing in node metrics: nvidia-smi on some MIG nodes shows GPUs 100% memory used by `kubelet` and driver-reserved — likely miscalculated allocatable mem during kubelet boot. Example:
```
$ kubectl exec -it node-3 -- nvidia-smi
| GPU 0 : MIG 0c - 0.25g |  Used Memory: 6144 MiB / 8192 MiB |
```
kai: That indicates kubelet reserve settings might be aggressive for MIG devices; we should run `kubelet --v=2` logs and check device-plugin versions. Could be device-plugin not reporting proper allocatable due to mismatched driver+plugin.
anya: I'll roll a small device-plugin restart on MIG nodegroup to attempt recalculation (daemonset rolling restart). Doing a 30s rolling restart.
anya: Restarted device-plugin on 8 nodes. allocatable values recalculated; several nodes now report 1.0 allocatable. Those freed GPUs accepted pending pods.
sara: Metrics: queue down to ~1200. 429s decreasing. Latency SLO still degraded for 15m window, but trending back.
dana: Customer support: CS notified enterprise tenants of mitigation and ETA for full recovery.
kai: Root cause hypothesized: combination of (A) mixed nodegroups with different MIG profiles, (B) autoscaler hitting ASG cap so no new full-GPU nodes, and (C) device-plugin / kubelet allocatable mismatch leaving some GPUs appearing fractional-only. That created stranded capacity and scheduler couldn't place whole-GPU pods -> queue growth and throttling.
mike: Next steps (post-incident):
  - Short: change expander to prefer full-gpu groups, add toleration for preemption, temporary increase ASG max, and fix device-plugin restart on boot.
  - Medium: implement fractional-GPU aware scheduler or enable Multi-Instance scheduling (allow pods to consume N slices), and add autoscaler rules that consider MIG fragmentation.
  - Long: better test harnesses for mixed-MIG deployments and autoscaler scale-limit scenarios.

kai: For immediate: I requested ASG quota bump and adjusted asg-gpu-prod-full max to 180 (was 150) — pending approvals. Also set expander to `largest` and restarted cluster-autoscaler.
ops-bot: autoscaler: restarted at 14:33:05 by kai
sara: Confirming 429 rate back to baseline. Gateway routes stable.
dana: Filing incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime (Anya) for follow-up on device-plugin and scheduler changes. Marking priority P1 -> P2 for follow-ups.
kai: On-call handoff: I’ll be on shift for 30 more mins, then @mike takes over. Mike, please monitor queue and ASG approval ticket.
mike: Taking over in 30. Set an alert to reopen paging if queue > 2k for 10m.
incident-bot: incident 1763401200 resolved by mitigation actions at 14:43:07 (status: mitigated)
dana: Thanks everyone. Postmortem draft coming — include timeline, commands run, and customer impact table.
anya: Leaving notes in the incident doc: device-plugin restart fixed several nodes; adding a startup probe to ensure correct allocatable before marking node ready.
kai: Good call. Closing live thread but keep channel pinned to incident doc for postmortem edits.
